messages:
zach: quick heads-up: kicked off an ad-hoc recompute for last-week aggregates and noticed many finished fast but a handful returned slightly different values vs the golden store. look like prefetch/cache was used during recompute. anyone else hit cache-driven drift? :thinking:
mira: saw this in staging earlier. our heuristic allows KV-prefetch for shards > 1M keys to avoid full-scan. speedups are great but customers noticed small deltas on high-cardinality keys.
ted: can you paste an example diff? curious how big the divergence is.
zach: example small sample:
```
agg_key=signup_source:email
full_recompute=12483
cached-prefetch=12473
delta=-10 (0.08%)
```

mira: that's within expectations for prefetched prefix merges but we didn't make that explicit in Console or in the recompute API. UX gap.
fran: two questions: (1) should recompute default to strict (no prefetch) for paid accounts? (2) if we keep prefetch, how do we surface "may differ" to users clearly in the UI and logs?
ted: ops viewpoint: full recompute costs ~3x and takes longer. many customers pick recompute for freshness only, not absolute parity, so a cheaper "fast" mode is appealing. but we need clear opt-in and traceability.
mira: proposal: add recompute_mode with values [strict, fast_prefetch, approximate] to the API. Console shows radio buttons with inline expected runtime and estimated token/compute cost. default for self-serve = fast_prefetch, enterprise = strict. behind a feature flag for now.
zach: logging: include recompute_mode in every audit line and append a small claim in artifacts: "mode_used=fast_prefetch, estimated_drift=0.1%" so support can triage.
fran: routing/policy: when mode=strict we should avoid preemptible workers and prefer dedicated lanes; tag with routing-policy=recompute:strict to ensure low-noise execution. Need to ensure quotas/caps reflect this.
ted: also add a Console hover that shows an example diff for the top 5 keys if mode != strict. one-click "show diff" after job completes. useful for product.
mira: telemetry plan: for every recompute emit event {mode, tenant_id, shard_count, runtime_ms, cost_estimate, average_abs_delta_pct}. We'll create a Console dashboard tile: recompute mode adoption, avg drift by mode, cost by mode, and top-ten tenants with highest drift.
fran: canary: run fast_prefetch vs strict on 8 tenants and compare top-20 keys. if median drift <0.2% we can keep fast_prefetch default for self-serve. infra-bot, schedule a canary and tag #eng-sre.
infra-bot: canary-scheduler: scheduled dry-run at 5532414800 for tenant set "prefetch-canary-8". Notifying #eng-platform and #eng-sre. :white_check_mark:
zach: UX copy: Console job detail should show a small badge "mode: fast (may differ)" and a link "how differences are computed". please make copy as non-technical as possible.
ted: runbook updates: how to detect drift complaints, how to re-run strict recompute, and billing reconciliation if fallback to dedicated was used. I'll draft and PR.
mira: infra asks we add a soft quota for strict mode to avoid Dedicated swamping on spikes and a fallback policy that asks for explicit consent in Console.
fran: one more: add an experiment flag to surface default mode per-account tier so Product can test conversion.
zach: OK I'll open RFC + Console mock + telemetry schema. tagging @mira for API + router flags and @ted for runbook. rolling this behind a feature flag until canary wraps. :rocket:
